questions.q: The figure shows two diagrams of the same screw gauge. In the first case, nothing is kept in its jaw and in the second case a small ball is kept between the jaws for which the diameter is required to be measured. The number of circular divisions on the shown screw gauge is $50$. It moves $0 . 5mm$ on the main scale for one complete rotation and the main scale has $\dfrac{1}{2}mm$ marks. The diameter of the ball& is
questions.solution:
$\text{Pitch} = \text{0.5 mm}$

$\text{L.C} = \dfrac{\text{0.5}}{\text{50}}$

$= \text{0.01 mm}$

$\text{M.S.R = 2}$

Neck reading = 25

$\text{d} = 2 \times \left(\text{0.5}\right) + \text{25} \times \text{0.01}$

$= \text{1.25 mm}$

Considering zero error

Here zero error is

$= + 5 \times \text{0.01}$

$= + \text{0.05 mm}$

so actual diameter

$= \text{d} - \text{0.05}$

$= \text{1.20 mm}$

$ε = xl$

$ε = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}l}{L} ∴ ε = \dfrac{E}{100} \times 30$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two tangent galvanometers having coils of the same radius are connected in series. A current flowing in them produces deflections of $60 °$ and $45 °$ respectively. The ratio of the number of turns in the coil is -
questions.solution:
In series, current is same in tangent galvanometer.

$B = {B}_{H}tan\theta ⇒ \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}ni}{2R} = {B}_{H}tan\theta$

$∵ i$ is same

$∴ n ∝ tan\theta ⇒ \dfrac{n1}{n2} = \dfrac{tan60 °}{tan45 °} = \dfrac{3}{1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The deflection in a moving coil galvanometer is
options: directly proportional to the torsional constant
directly proportional to the number of turns in the coil
inversely proportional to the area of the coil
inversely proportional to the current flowing
questions.solution:
Deflection is directly proportional to electric current in moving coil galvanometer.

$i = \dfrac{k}{nBA}\theta ⇒ \theta = \dfrac{nBA}{k}i ⇒ \theta ∝ n$

questions.q: The mean time period of second's pendulum is $2.00s$ and mean absolute error in the time period is $0.05s$. To express maximum estimate of error, the time period should be written as
questions.solution:
Mean time period $T = 2.00s$~and Mean absolute error $= \Delta T = 0.05s$

To express maximum estimate of error, the time period should be written as $\left(2.0 \pm 0.05\right)s$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cooling curve is plotted between the temperature of a hot body and time. Which of the following is not true for the cooling curve?
options: Cooling is faster from a calorimeter having a larger surface area than a smaller one.
Cooling is faster from a calorimeter painted black from outside than that from a polished surfaced calorimeter.
Cooling is faster from a copper calorimeter than from a steel calorimeter.
The rate of cooling remains same throughout the experiment. Hence the graph is a straight line.
questions.solution: The rate of cooling is faster at the beginning and then decreases and becomes constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the radius of a sphere is measured to be $( 2. 1 \pm 0. 05 ) cm.$ Calculate the surface area (in ${cm}^{2}$ ).
questions.solution:
$S = 4{\pi r}^{2} = 4 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times ( 2 . 1{)}^{2}$

$= 55 . 44{cm}^{2}$

$\dfrac{\Delta S}{S} = 2\left(\dfrac{\Delta r}{r}\right)$

$\Delta S = 2\left(\dfrac{\Delta r}{r}\right)S$

$= \dfrac{2 \times 0 . 05 \times 55 . 44}{2 . 1} = 2 . 64$

$∴ \Delta S = ( 55 . 44 \pm 2 . 64 ) {cm}^{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A battery of emf $12V$ and internal resistance $2Ω$ is connected in series with a tangent galvanometer of resistance $4Ω.$ The deflection is ${60}^{o}$ when the plane of the coil is along the magnetic meridian. To get a deflection of ${30}^{o},$ the resistance to be connected in series with the tangent galvanometer is
questions.solution:
$I = ktan ⁡ \theta,k$ being reduction factor and $I ∝ \dfrac{1}{R}$

$⇒ \dfrac{R + r}{\left(R + r\right) + R^{′}} = \dfrac{tan ⁡ {\theta}^{′}}{tan ⁡ \theta}$

$⇒ \dfrac{4 + 2}{6 + R^{′}} = \dfrac{tan ⁡ {30}^{o}}{tan ⁡ {60}^{o}}$

$⇒ R^{′} = 12Ω$
